title: The Prashna Upanishad, with Shankara's commentary
attributionNote: Anonymous, and belonging to the Pippalada school of the Atharvaveda; the teaching is given to six questioners by the teacher Pippalada. The commentary beside the text is ascribed to Shankara.
description: Six students come to the sage Pippalada and each asks a question: where are all beings born from, how many powers keep the body, what is the relation of breath to the self, what sleeps and what watches in sleep, what is meditation, and what is the sixteen-part person. The answers move through the hierarchy of the senses and the breaths to the one who is the seer, and close with the counsel that this teaching is not to be given to anyone who has not lived it.
historicalContext: Coming from the Atharvaveda, the Prashna is one of the later additions to the principal ten, and is read with the Mundaka and Mandukya in the Vedanta schools.
availabilityNote: Complete: all six questions, sixty-seven units of the GRETIL e-text, streamed at read time one question at a time, with the commentary ascribed to Shankara in a second pane.
